notes_for_editor: 1) Thin station: no build date, builder, keeper or event is in any source found. The Lighthouse Directory says 'Date unknown'. The local report corpus (Canadian Marine annual reports, 1900 to 1925) does not name the light, so its history may begin later; a human could check the Coast Guard's own records or the Lasqueti Island Historical Society. 2) The KnowBC preview shows that the James Sangster biography is inside the Sangster Island entry itself, not in a following entry; the preview does not say how the island was named, and the story does not claim the naming. KnowBC is subscription-only, so only the public preview was read. 3) The Wikipedia list of BC lighthouses gives a 'Sangster Island Light' row with no clear build year; it is a lead only and not cited. 4) The record's coordinates (49.423397, -124.192859) match the Coast Guard list (49 25 25.3 N, 124 11 34.9 W). 5) Rowlett's '5 m (17 ft) round tower' is kept as the Directory gives it; the source does not say whether it is height or diameter, so the story does not call it a height. 6) The Coast Guard list gives 'Q R 1s' and the Directory 'quick-flashing red'; the OSM 'Fl R 4s' is not supported by either official source. 7) Fact-check 2026-10-28: the story now says the Directory gives the tower as 5 m (17 ft) round, names the biography as inside the island entry, and footnotes every factual sentence.
